summary30s: The 1967 Fourth General Elections were a 'political earthquake': Congress lost power in 9 states and suffered its lowest Lok Sabha majority (283 seats).
Socialist leader Ram Manohar Lohia formulated 'Non-Congressism', uniting ideologically disparate opposition parties into Samyukta Vidhayak Dal (SVD) coalitions.
The 1967 elections popularized 'Aya Ram Gaya Ram', coined after Haryana MLA Gaya Lal switched parties thrice in a fortnight.

In 1969, the Congress split into Congress (O) led by the 'Syndicate' and Congress (R) led by Indira Gandhi, triggered by the presidential election where independent V.V. Giri defeated official nominee N. Sanjiva Reddy.
In 1971, Indira Gandhi dissolved the Lok Sabha and scored a landslide victory (375 seats with CPI) on the slogan 'Garibi Hatao', completely restoring Congress dominance.

coreConcepts.title: The 1967 Elections: 'Political Earthquake' & Non-Congressism
coreConcepts.explanation: The Fourth General Elections (February 1967) took place amidst economic crisis, two drought years, inflation, and two Prime Ministerial successions (Nehru died May 1964; Shastri died Jan 1966). Socialist leader Ram Manohar Lohia coined the strategy of 'Non-Congressism', arguing that Congress rule was undemocratic and pro-rich, and non-Congress parties must unite despite ideological divergence. The results were described as a 'political earthquake': Congress lost in 9 states (Punjab, Haryana, UP, MP, Bihar, West Bengal, Orissa, Madras, and Kerala). In Madras, DMK won a clear majority on its own (anti-Hindi agitation), becoming the first non-Congress party to win a state majority.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 5, Section 2
coreConcepts.examTip: DMK in Madras was the first regional non-Congress party to secure a clear majority on its own in any state assembly (1967).

coreConcepts.title: Coalitions (SVD) and 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram'
coreConcepts.explanation: The 1967 elections inaugurated the era of coalition politics at the state level. Non-Congress parties joined hands to form coalition governments known as 'Samyukta Vidhayak Dal' (SVD). In UP, former Congress leader Charan Singh formed the first SVD government. The election also brought political defections to national prominence, giving birth to the famous phrase 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram'. The phrase originated from Gaya Lal, an MLA in Haryana, who changed his party three times in a single fortnight in 1967. Defections caused rapid falls of state ministries, leading to the eventual Anti-Defection Act in 1985 (52nd Amendment).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 5, Section 2
coreConcepts.examTip: The phrase 'Aya Ram Gaya Ram' originated from Haryana MLA Gaya Lal in 1967.

coreConcepts.title: The Syndicate and the Great Split of 1969
coreConcepts.explanation: The 'Syndicate' was an informal group of powerful senior Congress leaders who controlled the party machine: K. Kamaraj (former CM Tamil Nadu), S.K. Patil (Bombay), S. Nijalingappa (Karnataka, Congress President), Atulya Ghosh (West Bengal), and N. Sanjiva Reddy (Andhra). They had installed Indira Gandhi as PM in 1966 assuming she would depend on them. Instead, Indira assertively adopted a radical left-populist agenda (Ten-Point Programme: nationalisation of 14 banks, abolition of Privy Purses). When President Zakir Hussain died in May 1969, the Syndicate nominated N. Sanjiva Reddy as the official Congress presidential candidate. Indira Gandhi covertly encouraged Vice-President V.V. Giri to run as an independent candidate, calling for a 'conscience vote'. V.V. Giri won. Congress President Nijalingappa expelled Indira Gandhi, splitting the party into Congress (O) / Organisation and Congress (R) / Requisitionists.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 5, Section 3
coreConcepts.examTip: 1969 Presidential contest: Official Congress candidate N. Sanjiva Reddy defeated by independent candidate V.V. Giri backed by Indira Gandhi.

coreConcepts.title: The 1971 Lok Sabha Elections and Congress Restoration
coreConcepts.explanation: Reduced to a minority government supported from outside by the CPI and DMK, Indira Gandhi dissolved the Lok Sabha in December 1970. All major non-communist, non-Congress opposition parties formed the 'Grand Alliance' (SSP, PSP, Bharatiya Jana Sangh, Swatantra, Congress(O)). The Grand Alliance had an anti-Indira agenda with the slogan 'Indira Hatao' (Remove Indira). Indira Gandhi counter-attacked with a positive, socialist welfare slogan: 'Garibi Hatao' (Remove Poverty). The results were a landslide: the Congress(R)-CPI alliance won 375 seats (Congress alone 352 seats with 44% vote), while the Grand Alliance won less than 40 seats. Following the December 1971 victory in Bangladesh, Indira Gandhi's authority was absolute, completely restoring the Congress system, albeit centralized around her personality.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 5, Section 4
coreConcepts.examTip: 1971 slogans: Opposition = 'Indira Hatao'; Indira Gandhi = 'Garibi Hatao'. Congress(R) won 352 seats.

workedExamples.question:
Which socialist thinker formulated the political strategy of 'Non-Congressism' prior to the 1967 Fourth General Elections?
(A) Acharya Narendra Deva
(B) Ram Manohar Lohia
(C) Jayaprakash Narayan
(D) C. Rajagopalachari
workedExamples.explanation: Ram Manohar Lohia gave this strategy the name of 'non-Congressism'. He argued that Congress rule was undemocratic and opposed to the interests of ordinary poor people.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Identify the strategy of uniting non-Congress parties in 1967.
Step 2: Formulated by socialist ideologue Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia.
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Direct strategy attribution from NCERT Chapter 5.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify the strategy of uniting non-Congress parties in 1967.
Step 2: Formulated by socialist ideologue Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia.

workedExamples.question:
In the 1969 Presidential election that precipitated the formal split of the Congress, whom did Indira Gandhi endorse against the official Congress candidate N. Sanjiva Reddy?
(A) V.V. Giri
(B) Zakir Hussain
(C) Morarji Desai
(D) Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed
workedExamples.explanation: Indira Gandhi encouraged the then Vice-President, V.V. Giri, to file his nomination as an independent candidate, and called for a 'conscience vote', leading to V.V. Giri's victory over the Syndicate's candidate N. Sanjiva Reddy.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Official Syndicate candidate = N. Sanjiva Reddy.
Step 2: Indira Gandhi backed independent candidate = V.V. Giri.
Step 3: Giri won, triggering the split into Congress (O) and Congress (R).
workedExamples.cuetPattern: Pivotal political turning points and factional confrontation.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Official Syndicate candidate = N. Sanjiva Reddy.
Step 2: Indira Gandhi backed independent candidate = V.V. Giri.
Step 3: Giri won, triggering the split into Congress (O) and Congress (R).

commonTraps.misconception: Thinking Congress (O) was Indira Gandhi's faction.
commonTraps.correctConcept: Congress (O) stood for Congress (Organisation), led by the old-guard Syndicate. Indira Gandhi's faction was Congress (R) for Congress (Requisitionists).
commonTraps.cuetWarning: Congress (O) = Syndicate (Old guard); Congress (R) = Indira Gandhi (Requisitionists).

commonTraps.misconception: Believing the Grand Alliance included the Communist Party of India (CPI).
commonTraps.correctConcept: The CPI was in an alliance WITH Indira Gandhi's Congress(R). The Grand Alliance was formed by non-communist opposition parties (Jana Sangh, Swatantra, PSP, SSP, Congress-O).
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Questions ask which party was allied with Indira Gandhi in 1971.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: CPI was allied with Congress (R); Grand Alliance opposed both.

practiceQuestions.question: Who was the political leader who coined the strategy and slogan of 'Non-Congressism' prior to the 1967 elections?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Ram Manohar Lohia formulated the theoretical and tactical justification for Non-Congressism.

practiceQuestions.question: In the 1967 assembly elections, which regional party became the first non-Congress party to secure a clear majority on its own in any state?

options.text: Bharatiya Kranti Dal in Uttar Pradesh

practiceQuestions.explanation: In Madras State (now Tamil Nadu), the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) won a clear majority on its own.

practiceQuestions.question: From which state did the MLA Gaya Lal belong, whose rapid floor-crossing gave rise to the phrase 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram' in 1967?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Gaya Lal was an MLA from Haryana who changed his party thrice in a fortnight.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match the leader of the Congress 'Syndicate' in List-I with their home state in List-II:
List-I:
(A) K. Kamaraj
(B) S.K. Patil
(C) S. Nijalingappa
(D) Atulya Ghosh

List-II:
1. Bombay (Maharashtra)
2. Tamil Nadu
3. West Bengal
4. Karnataka
practiceQuestions.explanation: Kamaraj: Tamil Nadu; S.K. Patil: Bombay; Nijalingappa: Karnataka; Atulya Ghosh: West Bengal.

practiceQuestions.question: In the 1969 Presidential election, whom did Indira Gandhi call upon party members to vote for according to their 'conscience'?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Indira Gandhi openly supported Vice-President V.V. Giri as an independent candidate, calling for a 'conscience vote' against the official candidate Sanjiva Reddy.

practiceQuestions.question: What was the famous campaign slogan of Indira Gandhi in the 1971 Lok Sabha elections that countered the opposition's 'Indira Hatao'?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Indira Gandhi gave the positive slogan 'Garibi Hatao' (Remove Poverty), focusing on land ceilings, bank nationalisation, and employment.

practiceQuestions.question: Following the 1969 split, which faction of the Congress was led by the Syndicate under S. Nijalingappa?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The faction led by the Syndicate came to be known as Congress (O) or Congress (Organisation), while Indira Gandhi's faction was Congress (R) or Requisitionists.

practiceQuestions.question: In July 1969, how many major commercial banks were nationalized by the Indira Gandhi government in a landmark socialist policy decision?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Indira Gandhi government nationalized 14 major private commercial banks in July 1969.

practiceQuestions.question: The 'Grand Alliance' formed in the 1971 elections to defeat Indira Gandhi consisted of which of the following groups of parties?

options.text: SSP, PSP, Bharatiya Jana Sangh, Swatantra Party, and Congress (O)
Congress (R), CPI, DMK, and Akali Dal
Janata Party, Lok Dal, and Congress (S)

practiceQuestions.explanation: The Grand Alliance brought together SSP, PSP, BJS, Swatantra Party, and the Congress (O).

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The Congress system restored by Indira Gandhi after 1971 was fundamentally different from the Congress system of the Nehru era.
Reason (R): While the Nehruvian Congress was an inclusive umbrella coalition accommodating multiple autonomous factions, the post-1971 Congress was highly centralized and dependent almost entirely on the supreme personal popularity of Indira Gandhi.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Indira Gandhi transformed the nature of the Congress: internal factional democracy was replaced by high command centralization. Both are true and (R) explains (A).
